title: Spec 'Always' constraint unmet: modes never restyle host/router tones (only roofs)
evidence: spec-7-3-accessibility-core.md:25: "Every mode restyles ALL of the view: state triad, lanes, ghost, roofs/host/router tones, packet class colors, water/coast/park map tokens, wire ribbons/crisis outline." palette.odin:36-53 Palette_Token enum: "State_Healthy, State_Congested, State_Critical, Lane_Express, Lane_Standard, Lane_Best_Effort, Ghost_Ok, Ghost_Bad, Pipe_Copper, Pipe_Steel, Pipe_Fiber, Route_Glow, Route_Tie, Water, Park, Coast," (no Host/Router tokens; no mode table in data/palette.json lists host_body/host_roof/router_body/router_dark/router_led). view.odin:670-671: "rl.DrawRectangleV({c.x - w/2, c.y - h/2 + s*0.12}, {w, h - s*0.12}, p.host_body)" / "rl.DrawRectangleV({c.x - w/2, c.y - h/2}, {w, s * 0.28}, p.host_roof)"; view.odin:804-805: "rl.DrawCircleV(c, r, p.router_body)" / "rl.DrawCircleV(c, r * 0.45, p.router_dark)".
detail: Spec constraint says every mode restyles 'roofs/host/router tones'. Only house_roofs is remapped; host_body/host_roof/router_body/router_dark/router_led are absent from the token enum and all three tables, so they render canon under every mode.
recommended_fix: Add Host_Body/Host_Roof/Router_* to Palette_Token + the three mode tables (re-run the derivation script + palcheck), or amend the spec constraint.

title: still present since round 1: parity scenarios never run under any a11y mode or scale
evidence: parity.odin:182-184: "pal := rnd.palette_load()" / "view.palette = &pal" / "rnd.view_compute(&view, 1280, 720, &cat.balance)" — drive_parity and run_input_parity never set a Palette_Mode, reduced_motion, or ui_scale; every scenario runs at Off/1.0. Job briefing Acceptance 1: "input parity holds under every mode".
detail: AC 'input parity holds under every mode' is construction-argued only: chip rects are mode/scale-dependent (chip text varies by mode; hud() moves rects), yet no parity leg exercises any mode or x1.50.
recommended_fix: Drive the parity matrix once per a11y mode (or at minimum x1.50) so chip/row hit rects are exercised under restyle.

title: still present since round 1: spec's 1152x648 min-window scale AC has no exercising path
evidence: spec-7-3 line 47: "| Scale ×1.50 at min window 1152×648 | panel stepper | top band (health card, forecast, crisis banner), QoS panel, tray, caption strip never overlap | layout clamps, AC-pinned |"; line 92: "Given scale ×1.50 at 1152×648, then no HUD overlap anywhere". hud_test.odin:71-72 (the only clamp pin): "v.win_w = 1280" / "v.win_h = 720"; the harness renders every demo at 1280x720 (parity.odin:184).
detail: The banner clamp is unit-pinned at 1280 width only; no test, golden, or parity leg exercises 1152x648, so the spec's 'AC-pinned' claim for the min window is unverified. x1.25 rect math is now pinned (partial r1 relief).
recommended_fix: Add one crisis_card_width/tray clamp test at win_w=1152 (win_h=648), or a harness width flag + golden; else un-pin the claim.

title: still present since round 1: 'muted != silent' captions contract unpinned despite spec's 'pin it'
evidence: spec-7-3 line 51: "| Muted audio + alert | 7.2 seam | caption strip still captions (muted ≠ silent) | existing contract, pin it |". audio_test.odin contains only: "test_consumer_crisis_draw", "test_consumer_arrival_throttle", "test_caption_crisis_priority", "test_caption_expiry_and_reset", "test_wav_pack_header", "test_synth_wav_forms", "test_variant_draws_stay_in_range" — no mute case anywhere in the file.
detail: Spec I/O matrix explicitly says 'pin it'; the behavior exists (audio.odin drops only sound when muted) but no test covers a muted run's captions, so a regression shipping silent-when-muted would pass CI.
recommended_fix: One audio_test case: toggle mute, fire crisis + arrival alerts, assert caption_live still returns both captions.

title: PR claim 'base palette is untouched byte-for-byte' is false at file level (whitespace reformat)
evidence: chunk-rest.patch: "-  \"state_congested\":  [242, 181, 68, 255]," / "-  \"state_critical\":[232, 69, 69, 255]," → "+  \"state_congested\": [242, 181, 68, 255]," / "+  \"state_critical\": [232, 69, 69, 255]," and "-  \"packet_dark\":  [28, 70, 120, 255]," → "+  \"packet_dark\":   [28, 70, 120, 255],". _pr_body.md: "the base palette is untouched byte-for-byte".
detail: Three base-palette lines were reformatted (alignment only; values identical, goldens unaffected). The 'byte-for-byte untouched' PR claim is inaccurate for anyone diffing the file.
recommended_fix: Re-word the claim to 'token values unchanged (whitespace-normalized)' or revert the three whitespace edits.

title: still present since round 1: palcheck picks 40-vs-48 threshold by pr[0] color-value equality, not pair identity
evidence: palcheck.odin:126-129: "threshold := f32(48)" / "if (pr[0] == p.water || pr[0] == p.park || pr[0] == p.coast || pr[0] == p.canvas) {" / "threshold = 40" / "}".
detail: If a future mode edit sets a signal token equal to a map token's value, that pair silently falls under the looser 40 threshold — the oracle under-tests without failing loudly.
recommended_fix: Key the threshold on the pair's token indices (tag pairs as signal/map when appended), not color equality.

title: still present since round 1: malformed mode-table entry applies opaque BLACK, not the spec's base fallback
evidence: palette.odin:311-317: "tok, ok := palette_token_by_name(name)" / "if !ok { continue }" / "if arr, okq := v.(json.Array); okq {" / "i := int(tok)" / "t.set[i] = true" / "t.colors[i] = jcol_arr(arr, {0, 0, 0, 255})" / "}". spec-7-3 line 50: "| palette.json mode table malformed | palette_load | base palette fallback (jcol precedent) | palcheck flags the mode loudly |".
detail: A wrong-length or non-integer token entry sets set[i]=true with the {0,0,0,255} default — the mode applies opaque black instead of keeping base, contradicting the I/O matrix row's promised fallback.
recommended_fix: Only set t.set[i] when jcol_arr succeeds (pass the base color as default, or validate length/ints first).

title: still present since round 1: spec-7-3 doc drifts from shipped code (intent names, 0.99 pin, demo verb)
evidence: spec line 65: "new Intents (Settings_Toggle, Panel_Navigate, Panel_Activate, Scale_Step); mapped on all devices" — types.odin ships "Toggle_Settings :: struct {}", "Settings_Navigate :: struct { delta: i32 }", "Settings_Activate :: struct { delta: i32 }" (no Scale_Step). Line 67: "`a11y <mode>[,<mode>]` demo verb" — demo.odin implements subcommands "a11y palette <name> | a11y reduced | a11y scale <pct>". Line 106: "a fixed mid-envelope factor (e.g. 0.99)" — shipped pin is full static width.
detail: The frozen-after-approval spec names intents, a reduced-motion value, and a demo verb that all differ from the shipped code; future readers get three wrong pointers.
recommended_fix: True up the three spec lines to the shipped names (Toggle_Settings/Settings_Navigate/Settings_Activate, full-static pin, subcommand verb).

evidence: palcheck.odin:414: "modes := []rnd.Palette_Mode{.Deutan, .Protan, .Tritan}" — the section-4 presence loop scans only the three palette modes' frames; a11y_reduced/a11y_scale rely solely on the T2 byte-hash (initial-bless validity was a one-off vision-read, not a gate).
